answer: Add/Drop Groups are addressed as adg-<adg-number>, where adg-number is an integer in the range [1..110], so a node can have up to 110 ADGs (add adg-1 creates one; delete adg-<n> removes it). Whether the same wavelength can appear twice is reported by the show-only attribute wavelength-duplication, which says whether the SRG can handle duplicate wavelengths and to what extent. Its values are one-per-adg (no duplication of frequencies in the ADG) and one-per-degree (CDC: duplication of frequencies allowed in the ADG, but only one at the Degree). The default is one-per-adg, and only CDCs allow more than one instance of the same wavelength on the ADG. Other show attributes are label (String 0..256), max-add-drop-ports and bands-supported (default standardC-band).

On set amplifier-<name>, control-mode selects auto-max-pw (default, the auto mode targeting maximum output power) or manual. In manual control mode you set gain-target, range 0..40 dB, default 0.0, used to set the gain for constant-gain mode; gain-operating reports the actually configured gain over the same 0..40 dB range. In auto control mode you do not set the gain; instead gain-adjustment applies a user offset in the range [-20.00..20.00], default 0, and it is only supported on amplifiers whose function is pa or inline. Tilt is controlled by tilt-control-mode with values manual, auto (default, system implicitly controls tilt per configured fiber parameters) and auto-planned (system controls tilt per planning tool parameters), so by default the system does control tilt itself. tilt-target ([-5..5] dB, default 0dB) applies only to manual mode and raises the warning that the attribute may be traffic affecting; tilt-adjustment ([-5..5] dB, default 0dB) offsets the target when tilt-control-mode is auto or auto-planned. When the amplifier function is add or drop, the only tilt option is manual.

Use set amplifier-raman-<name> target-raman-gain <value>. The permitted range is [0, 5..30dB] with default 0dB, so you ask for either 0 or a value from 5 to 30 dB. It is configurable only when control-mode is different than auto; when control-mode is auto the parameter is ignored. control-mode values are auto (you configure only the span attributes and optionally the pointloss, gain is controlled automatically), auto-planned (you configure the target Raman gain plus span attributes) and manual (basic manual configuration, even the target pump powers must be configured); the default is auto. To see how many pumps the card has, use show amplifier-raman-<name> number-of-pumps: it reports the number of pumps for the required-equipped card, either 4 or 2, and that value dictates the number of pump-power objects exposed by the system. total-pump-power reports the operating total pump power over [-99..99 dBm], where -99 means no power.

Switch ASE loading on with set ase-idler-service-<name> ase-idler-enable enabled, for example set ase-idler-service-1-8 ase-idler-enable enabled. ase-idler-enable takes enabled or disabled and defaults to disabled; enabled turns on ASE idler signal filling on the unused and nmc-failed portions of the band spectrum. The attribute can also be given on the add ase-idler-service-<name> command, along with alarm-report-control (allowed default, or inhibited). To see whether it actually came up, read the show-only attribute ase-idler-state with show ase-idler-service-<name> ase-idler-state. Its values are ase-enabled (ASE idler signal filling is complete on the band spectrum), ase-partially-enabled (filling is incomplete), ase-faulted (the ASE idler signal is faulted) and ase-disabled (the signal is completely removed from the band spectrum), with default ase-disabled. oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled) and avail-state are also available.

The ASE source output power is set with set ase-idler-source-<name> target-output-power <value>. It is the ASE pump output power required if manually configured, with permitted range (-3.00..20.50) dBm and a default of 13. The pump is not on by default: pump-enable takes enabled or disabled and defaults to disabled, so you must explicitly enable it. The read-only pump-state, which shows the state of the ASE Idler pump, is likewise enabled or disabled with default disabled. A single command can do both, for example set ase-idler-source-1-3.1-ase pump-enable 'enabled' target-output-power '15.00'. Other settable attributes are admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), label (String 0..256) and alarm-report-control (allowed default, or inhibited). The function attribute is fixed at ase-idler-source.

Use the calibrate command, which runs in Operational Mode only, with the syntax calibrate [type=]<value> [trigger=]<value> [entity=]<value>. type has the single value raman, which triggers calibration on raman cards. trigger has the values start, which starts the Raman gain calibration for the OTS span, and stop, which stops it. entity selects the entity to be calibrated and depends on the type parameter; for raman calibration the entity may be an OTS-R entity, given as an instance-identifier. None of the three parameters has a default. To trigger an automatic Raman gain calibration: calibrate raman start ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line. To stop one: calibrate raman stop ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line.

Degrees are addressed as degree-<degree-number>, where degree-number is an integer in the range [1..20] and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees, so a node can have up to 20 degrees (add degree-1 creates one). The spectral granularity is reported by show degree-<degree-number>: slot-width-granularity is the width of a slot with a default of 6250 (value in MHz), and center-freq-granularity, the granularity of allowed center frequencies, defaults to 3125 (value in MHz) with the base frequency for the computation being 193.1 THz per G.694.1. min-slots, the minimum number of slots that may be joined to form a media channel, defaults to 8, and max-slots, the maximum, defaults to 32; min-slots must be less than or equal to max-slots. Also shown are label, is-foadm (default false), wss-less (default true) and bands-supported (default standardC-band).

On a multi-rail ILA node the direction command assigns an index to each DWDM line port, and the system pairs them: direction n and direction n+1 are automatically assigned by the system to the DWDM Line1 and DWDM Line2 ports of the #n C2ILASGH/D2ILASGM card created, where index n is an odd integer with a value between 1 and 15. That is why they come in odd/even pairs: the DWDM Line1 port is always assigned an odd index value and the DWDM Line2 port is always assigned an even index value. The index range is [1..16] (1 and 2 are used when migrating from R6.x). The system sets direction-number from the configured direction-port: 1 when the port is dwdm-line1, 2 when it is dwdm-line2, default 1. direction-port must therefore be port-<shelf>-<slot>-dwdm-line1 for an odd index and port-<shelf>-<slot>-dwdm-line2 for an even index, and the same dwdm-line* port instance can only be selected once per NE. Create with add direction-1 direction-port port-1-3-dwdm-line1; delete -f forces without confirmation.

On a dsc facility the configurable attributes are the ones offered by add dsc-<name> and set dsc-<name>: label (String, length 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock) and alarm-report-control (allowed, meaning alarm reporting is allowed, or inhibited; default allowed). name is the file name without the .log extension, String length 0...128. Everything else is show only: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID (String 1..64), oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state and managed-by. The managed-by attribute describes whether this facility was system created or not; its values are system and user with a default of system, and only user-created facilities can be user deleted. So a dsc showing managed-by system cannot be removed with delete dsc-<name>.

On add dsc-group-<name> or set dsc-group-<name> there are four Q signal degrade attributes. Before FEC: pre-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold is the threshold on which the PRE-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE alarm is raised, decimal64 with 3 fraction digits, range 0|5.600..9.600 dB, where 0 implies threshold crossing alarming disabled and the specific sub-range is per carrier use-case; pre-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis is decimal64 with 1 fraction digit, range 0.1..1.0 dB, default 0.5. After FEC: post-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold raises POST-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE, decimal64 with 1 fraction digit, range (12.5..18.0) dB, default 18; post-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis is range (0.1..1.0) dB, default 0.5. Related is dgd-high-threshold, which raises the DGD-OORH alarm, uint16 range (25..400) ps, default 100. Example: add dsc-group-1-3-1-1 rate 100 carriers 1-3-1 group-id 1 instance-id 1.

Use the gadt command, which retrieves information about golden carrier application information. The syntax is show gadt [<application-description-H|application-description-P|application-description-S|application-description-U>], and it is available in both Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. The four parameters application-description-H, application-description-P, application-description-S and application-description-U each give a detailed description of an application ID and are of type string with no default. For example, show gadt application-description-H returns application-description 'Subsea modes using Uniform and Hybrid modulation'. The application IDs H, P, S and U are the same letters used in the application field of a golden carrier mode name such as 800M.95P.

The gapt command lists the golden advanced parameters from the Golden Advanced Parameters Table (GAPT), and it is scoped per card type. The syntax is show gapt-<card-type> [version] [applicable-resource-type], available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. card-type is the card type name (string), version is the table version (string, length 0..5), and applicable-resource-type is the managed resource type(s) applicable for that particular advanced parameter (string); none has a default. Plain show gapt lists the tables per card, for example gapt-CHM6 at version 1.8, gapt-CHM7 at version 3.0 and gapt-CHM7T. Scoping to one card, show gapt-chm7, lists that card's entries such as golden-advanced-parameter-CHM7/BOASetting, golden-advanced-parameter-CHM7/NLC and golden-advanced-parameter-CHM7/RxCDMode, followed by the table's version and applicable-resource-type.

Use the gcmt command, which retrieves information about the golden carrier mode. The syntax is show gcmt [<card-type>] [version], available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode; the object parameter is the golden carrier modes (string) and version is the table version (string), neither with a default. To look up a specific mode, name it directly: show gcmt golden-carrier-mode-800M.95P. The output lists the mode with its capacity (Gbps), client-mode, baud-rate (GBaud), application, compatibility-id and status, for example golden-carrier-mode-CHM6/800M.95P with capacity 800, client-mode ethernet-otn, baud-rate 95.2965203, application P, compatibility-id 6 and status supported. For the full per-attribute view use show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode>.

Read the status attribute with show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode> status, which describes the carrier mode release status. Its values are supported, candidate, experimental, deprecated and diagnostic, with no default, so a mode showing supported is fully supported while one showing experimental is not. The same status column appears in show gcmt output alongside capacity, client-mode, baud-rate, application and compatibility-id, for example golden-carrier-mode-CHM6/800M.95P with status supported. Two related attributes qualify this per subtype: supported-subtypes lists the subtypes that each carrier mode supports (string length 0...32, maximum 20 elements), and candidate-subtypes lists the subtypes for which this carrier mode has candidate status (string length 0..16, maximum 10 elements). Both the gcmt and golden-carrier-mode commands run in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use the l0-capabilities command, which shows the capabilities details related with the node's Layer 0 functions. The syntax is simply show l0-capabilities. It takes no command parameters at all, and it is available in both Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. For the photonic node's structural limits specifically, the companion command is show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs], which reports the maximum number of degrees (20) and the maximum number of ADGs (110).

A Media Channel is carved out with add mc-<name>, and three arguments are mandatory: parent-oms, lower-frequency and upper-frequency. parent-oms is an instance-identifier set only upon MC creation, and its referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree, it cannot be in an ADG. lower-frequency and upper-frequency are the lower and upper frequencies of the media channel, given as values in MHz. Optional arguments on add are label (String 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed default, or inhibited) and auto-delete (disabled default, or enabled; enabled is only allowed on RD66TM sleds with l0-mode-op=hsc-ols and is always disabled if l0-mode-op is standard or slte). The system derives center-frequency and slot-width, the latter calculated as upper-frequency minus lower-frequency. Example: add mc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 parent-oms '1-3.1-dwdm-line' lower-frequency '192225000' upper-frequency '192300000'.

The Media Channel Filler is read only. The mc-f command is used only to show the Media Channel Filler facility attributes, and its sole syntax is show mc-f-<name> [supporting-facilities] [supported-facilities] [supporting-card] [supporting-port] [AID] [lower-frequency] [upper-frequency] [slot-width]. There is no add, set or delete form, and every parameter in the table is marked as used in show only. The attributes are name (String 0..64), supporting-facilities and supported-facilities (instance identifiers to parent and children facilities), supporting-card and supporting-port (leafrefs), AID (String 1..64), lower-frequency and upper-frequency of the MC Filler in MHz units, and slot-width, calculated by the system from upper-frequency minus lower-frequency. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. By contrast, the Network Media Channel Filler command nmc-f does allow set of admin-state and alarm-report-control.

Cards are attached to an Add/Drop Group with add modules-adg-<adg-number>/<index> supported-card <value> [ocm-monitoring <value>]. adg-number is a number in the range [1..110] and index is a number in the range [1..4], so up to 4 cards can be put into one ADG. The card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). supported-card is the instance of the card for the ADG. Channel monitoring is on by default: ocm-monitoring takes true or false with a default of true. It is set upon creation and cannot be changed after supported-card has been assigned, but it can optionally be configured to false for OMD cards directly connected to PAx/BAX or C2ILASGH degrees, for example FOADM nodes. The command runs in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode for Network Administrator and Network Engineer. Example: add modules-adg-1/1 supported-card card-1-6.

Use add modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card <value>. degree-number is a number in the range [1..20] and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees. index has the single permitted value 1, and the card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). supported-card is an instance identifier for the card or subcard that belongs to the degree; in R6.0 the card must be RD09SM or RD20TM. You can afterwards change it with set modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card <value>, read it back with show modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> [supported-card], and remove the association with delete modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index>. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode, for Network Administrator and Network Engineer. Example: add modules-degree-1/1 supported-card card-1-1.

Use show monitored-channel-<name>/<frequency> monitored-optical-power. The name corresponds to the (WS04S) card name with the suffix -1 or -2, for ocm1-in or ocm2-in respectively, and frequency is the nominal center frequency of the carrier (channel) in MHz, a uint32. monitored-optical-power is the measured power for the corresponding carrier (channel) in dBm, decimal64 with range (-99.00..99.00) and default -99, where the value -99.00 means no power. The other show attribute is monitored-width, the carrier (channel) width configured at the NMC within the oxcon source/destination, in MHz, uint32, default 0. The command is show only, in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Example: show monitored-channel-1-1.2-ocm1-in/195987500 monitored-optical-power, or omit the attribute to see all of them.

On add nmc-<name>, center-frequency is mandatory and is the nominal center frequency of the NMC, with permitted values in the range [190650000..196700000] MHz. width is the network media channel frequency width in MHz, with values in the range [15000..200000] MHz and a default of 35000. The user must configure the 3 dB signal bandwidth, and the value in GHz must be equivalent to the baud rate in GBd configured on the connected transponder line interface line port. Both center-frequency and width are used in add and show only, so they are fixed at creation. The other mandatory creation argument is parent-facility, which can be either a Media Channel or an OMS, is only set upon creation, and whose referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree and cannot be in an ADG. Example: add nmc-cdc-1-4_192800000-34000 center-frequency 192800000 width 34000 parent-facility oms-1-4-ad1.

The Network Media Channel Filler occupies a default alloc-bandwidth of 75000, a value in MHz units, which is the allocated bandwidth of the NMC Filler. It is paired with alloc-lower-frequency and alloc-upper-frequency, the allocated lower and upper frequencies in MHz, neither of which has a default. The actually occupied spectrum is reported separately by actual-lower-frequency, actual-upper-frequency and actual-bandwidth, and actual-bandwidth defaults to 0. It is monitored: monitoring-state indicates whether the NMC is intended to be in use, and because this is a system created attribute it is enabled by default, with values enabled and disabled. All these are show only; on nmc-f only admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock) and alarm-report-control (allowed default, or inhibited) can be set. Power is read via power-actual-tx and power-actual-rx, each [-99.00..99.00] dBm with default -99. Example: show nmc-f-1-3-dwdm-line-58.

Use show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs], available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. max-degrees is the maximum number of degrees and reports 20 (uint8); it is 0 if not supported, degrees are only supported in OADM node types, and by convention the maximum degrees for the ILA node-type is 0 because an ILA has only 2 directions, fixedly, which is not shown in supported capabilities. The maximum number of degrees is not necessarily the deployment supported configuration, but the maximum number of a working degree-number. max-adgs is the maximum number of Add/Drop Groups and reports 110 (uint8); it is 0 if not supported, and ADGs are only supported in OADM node types. Typical output is max-degrees 20 and max-adgs 110. These match the degree-number range [1..20] and adg-number range [1..110].

On set oc-<name> the loopback attribute takes facility, terminal or none, with a default of none, and is useful to debug on the fiber connection; loopback-mode indicates the loopback action for facility or terminal and takes facility or terminal with no default. For test patterns, test-signal-type is the type of test pattern that is injected, with values none, enumeration, PRBS31Q, PRBS13Q, scrambled-idles, PRBS9 and PRBS31, defaulting to none. test-signal-direction is the direction of the test signal and has the single value ingress, default ingress. test-signal-monitoring monitors the incoming test signals for diagnostics and takes true or false, default false. All five attributes are readable through show oc-<name>. The command runs in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: set oc-1-5-T9.1 test-signal-monitoring false.

On an ILA node the OCHm represents the signaled optical channel from OSC, detected at the ILA OMS by using the OSC information; that is, the optical channel monitoring information is derived from the Optical Supervisory Channel rather than measured per channel locally. Consequently, when either the OMS monitoring-mode is not-monitored (as configured by the user), or there is no OSC messaging information, the list of OCHm facilities in the NE will be empty. Read the facilities with show ochm or show ochm-<name>, for example show ochm-1-7-dwdm-line2-191968750-egress avail-state. direction is ingress or egress but currently only egress is supported, default egress. power-actual is the currently received power in dBm, where -99dBm means the power is not yet measured (measurement is performed by the OCM at DGE2 card) or no power was detected; for egress it should be calibrated at the DWDM Line port output. Settable attributes are label, admin-state and alarm-report-control.
